children: By Takanori Yamamoto / Yomiuri Shimbun Correspondent

NEW YORK — Japanese conveyor belt sushi chain Sushiro will open its first U.S. outlet in October in Times Square, said Masahiro Yamamoto, president and CEO of operator Food & Life Companies Ltd., on Monday in New York.

The outlet will serve as the sushi chain's foothold to expand its business and build brand awareness in the United States, Yamamoto told reporters. "We expect the outlet to serve as a platform to promote (the brand) to the world," he added.

Sushiro has steadily increased its outlets in countries outside Japan such as China and Thailand. "Our foundation in Asia has become solid," Yamamoto said. Food & Life Companies now views the United States as a new growth market.

In 2024, Food & Life Companies opened a different style of sushi restaurant in Boston to study U.S. customer preferences and suitable management methods. The company now aims to leverage the insights gained at the Boston outlet to launch a full-scale entry into the U.S. market with its flagship Sushiro brand.
"The United States is the largest market in the world. We want to open a good number of stores," Yamamoto said. The company plans to open stores primarily along the East Coast.

In addition to tuna and salmon, much of the sushi to be offered at the Times Square outlet will be similar to stores in Japan. Prices will start at 5 dollars per plate, and tips will not be required. In New York, this is relatively affordable compared to typical sushi restaurants. "We will serve sushi at reasonable prices while maintaining high quality," Yamamoto said.
The Times Square outlet will have private rooms and a system allowing customers to order at their tables via large touchscreen panels to cater to a wide range of customers.
